sections.heading: Opening
paragraphs: Per the file, a Solana cluster uses (per the file) a multi-layer block propagation (per the file) mechanism called _Turbine_ to broadcast (per the file) ledger entries to all nodes. Per the file, the cluster divides itself (per the file) into layers of nodes, (per the file) and each node in (per the file) a given layer is (per the file) responsible for propagating any (per the file) data it receives on (per the file) to a small set (per the file) of nodes in the next downstream layer. Per the file, this way each node (per the file) only has to communicate (per the file) with a small number of nodes. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Layer Structure
paragraphs: Per the file, the leader communicates with (per the file) a special root node. Per the file, the root may be thought of as (per the file) layer 0 and communicates (per the file) with layer 1, which (per the file) is made up of (per the file) at most DATA_PLANE_FANOUT nodes. Per the file, if the number of (per the file) nodes in the cluster (per the file) is greater than layer (per the file) 1, then the data (per the file) plane fanout mechanism adds layers below.

Per the file, the number of nodes (per the file) in each additional layer (per the file) grows by a factor (per the file) of DATA_PLANE_FANOUT. Per the file, a good way to (per the file) think about this is, (per the file) layer 0 starts with (per the file) a single node, layer (per the file) 1 starts with fanout (per the file) nodes, and layer 2 (per the file) will have fanout * number (per the file) of nodes in layer (per the file) 1 and so on. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Layer Assignment  - Weighted Selection
paragraphs: Per the file, in order for data (per the file) plane fanout to work, (per the file) the entire cluster must (per the file) agree on how the (per the file) cluster is divided into layers. Per the file, to achieve this, all the recognized node nodes \(the TVU peers\) (per the file) are shuffled with a (per the file) stake weighting and stored in a list. Per the file, this list is then (per the file) indexed in different ways (per the file) to figure out layer (per the file) boundaries and retransmit peers (per the file) - referred to as the \(turbine tree\).

Per the file, for example, the list (per the file) is shuffled and leader (per the file) selects the first node (per the file) to be the root (per the file) node, and the root (per the file) node selects the next (per the file) DATA_PLANE_FANOUT nodes to make (per the file) up layer 1. Per the file, the shuffle is biased (per the file) towards higher staked nodes, (per the file) allowing heavier votes to (per the file) come back to the leader first.

Per the file, layer 2 and lower-layer (per the file) nodes use the same logic (per the file) to find their next layer peers. Per the file, to reduce the possibility (per the file) of attack vectors, the (per the file) list is shuffled and (per the file) indexed on every shred. Per the file, the turbine tree is (per the file) generated from the set of node nodes for each shred (per the file) using a seed derived (per the file) from the slot leader (per the file) id, slot, shred index, and shred type. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Configuration Values
paragraphs: Per the file, dATA_PLANE_FANOUT - Determines the size (per the file) of layer 1. Per the file, subsequent layers grow by (per the file) a factor of DATA_PLANE_FANOUT. Per the file, layers will fill to (per the file) capacity before new ones (per the file) are added, i.e if (per the file) a layer isn't full, it (per the file) _must_ be the last one. Per the file, currently, configuration is set (per the file) when the cluster is launched. Per the file, in the future, these (per the file) parameters may be hosted (per the file) on-chain, allowing modification on (per the file) the fly as the cluster sizes change. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Shred Propagation Flow
paragraphs: Per the file, during its slot, the (per the file) leader node makes its (per the file) initial broadcasts to a (per the file) special root node \(layer (per the file) 0\) sitting atop the turbine tree. Per the file, this root node is (per the file) rotated every shred based (per the file) on the weighted shuffle previously mentioned. Per the file, the root shares data with layer 1. Per the file, nodes in this layer (per the file) then retransmit shreds to (per the file) a subset of nodes (per the file) in the next layer \(layer 2\).

Per the file, in general, every node (per the file) in layer-1 retransmits to (per the file) a unique subset of nodes (per the file) in the next layer, etc, (per the file) until all nodes in the (per the file) cluster have received all the shreds. Per the file, to prevent redundant transmission, (per the file) each node uses the (per the file) deterministically generated turbine tree, (per the file) its own index in (per the file) the tree, and DATA_PLANE_FANOUT (per the file) to iterate through the tree and (per the file) identify downstream nodes.

Per the file, each node in a (per the file) layer only has to (per the file) broadcast its shreds to (per the file) a maximum of DATA_PLANE_FANOUT (per the file) nodes in the next layer instead (per the file) of to every TVU peer in (per the file) the cluster. sections.heading: Calculating the required FEC rate
paragraphs: Per the file, turbine relies on retransmission of packets between nodes. Per the file, due to retransmission, any (per the file) network wide packet loss (per the file) is compounded, and the (per the file) probability of the packet (per the file) failing to reach its (per the file) destination increases on each hop. Per the file, the FEC rate needs to take into acct the network wide packet (per the file) loss, and the propagation depth. Per the file, a shred group is (per the file) the set of data (per the file) and coding packets that may be used to reconstruct each other.

Per the file, each shred group has (per the file) a chance of failure, (per the file) based on the likelihood (per the file) of the number of (per the file) packets failing that exceeds the FEC rate. Per the file, if a node fails to reconstruct the (per the file) shred group, then the (per the file) block cannot be reconstructed, and the node has to rely on (per the file) repair to fixup the blocks. Per the file, the probability of the shred group failing may be computed using the binomial distribution.

Per the file, if the FEC rate (per the file) is 16:4, then the (per the file) group size is 20, and (per the file) at least 4 of the (per the file) shreds must fail for the (per the file) group to fail. Per the file, which is equal to (per the file) the sum of the (per the file) probability of 4 or (per the file) more trials failing out of 20.
